title: Judges Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who was Jephthah's mother according to Judges 11?
options: A harlot
A princess
A prophetess
A widow
questions.correctAnswer: A harlot
questions.explanation: Judges 11:1 states that Jephthah was the son of a harlot.

questions.question: Why did Jephthah's half-brothers thrust him out of his father's house?
options: Because he was the son of a strange woman
Because he was too young
Because he was lazy
Because he was poor
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was the son of a strange woman
questions.explanation: Judges 11:2 explains that his wife's sons said he was the son of a strange woman and so he should not inherit.

questions.question: Where did Jephthah flee to after he was thrust out by his brethren?
options: The land of Tob
The city of Jericho
The wilderness of Sinai
The land of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Tob
questions.explanation: Judges 11:3 says Jephthah fled and dwelt in the land of Tob.

questions.question: Who made war against Israel, prompting the elders to seek Jephthah's help?
options: The children of Ammon
The Philistines
The Moabites
The Edomites
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Ammon
questions.explanation: Judges 11:4 states that the children of Ammon made war against Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The elders of Gilead sent for Jephthah to be their captain to fight the children of Ammon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 11:5-6 shows that the elders of Gilead went to Tob to fetch Jephthah and asked him to be their captain.

questions.question: What was Jephthah’s initial reaction when the elders asked him to lead them?
options: He reminded them that they had previously hated and expelled him
He immediately accepted without hesitation
He demanded money first
He asked them to send a messenger instead
questions.correctAnswer: He reminded them that they had previously hated and expelled him
questions.explanation: Judges 11:7 records Jephthah questioning why they came to him now since they had expelled him before.

questions.question: True or False: The elders of Gilead promised Jephthah that if he fought and won, he would be their head over all inhabitants of Gilead.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 11:8 states the elders told Jephthah he would be their head if he went with them to fight.

questions.question: What condition did Jephthah place before agreeing to lead the fight against the children of Ammon?
options: That the LORD deliver the Ammonites into his hands
That he receive a large sum of gold
That his brothers apologize to him
That the elders swear loyalty to him forever
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD deliver the Ammonites into his hands
questions.explanation: Judges 11:9 shows Jephthah asking if he should be head only if the LORD delivers the Ammonites into his hands.

questions.question: What did the elders say to confirm their promise to Jephthah?
options: The LORD be witness between us
We swear on the river Jordan
We will build you a temple
We will crown you king immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD be witness between us
questions.explanation: Judges 11:10 records the elders saying 'The LORD be witness between us' confirming their promise.

questions.question: Where did Jephthah utter all his words before the LORD after becoming head and captain?
options: Mizpeh
Jerusalem
Hebron
Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpeh
questions.explanation: Judges 11:11 states Jephthah uttered all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh.

questions.question: What message did Jephthah send to the king of the children of Ammon?
options: What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land?
Surrender now or be destroyed
We will pay tribute to you
Let us make peace by marriage
questions.correctAnswer: What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land?
questions.explanation: Judges 11:12 records Jephthah's message questioning why the Ammonites came to fight in his land.

questions.question: True or False: The king of the children of Ammon claimed that Israel had taken his lands from Arnon to Jabbok and Jordan.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 11:13 shows the Ammonite king claimed Israel took his land from Arnon to Jabbok and Jordan.

questions.question: How did Jephthah respond to the claim that Israel took land from the children of Ammon?
options: He denied Israel took the land of Moab or Ammon
He admitted Israel took the land
He proposed a marriage to end the dispute
He asked for a ceasefire
questions.correctAnswer: He denied Israel took the land of Moab or Ammon
questions.explanation: Judges 11:15 states Jephthah said Israel did not take the land of Moab or Ammon.

questions.question: In the sequence of events, what happened first in Judges 11?
options: Jephthah was expelled by his brethren
The elders of Gilead sent for Jephthah
Jephthah vowed a vow to the LORD
The children of Ammon made war on Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Jephthah was expelled by his brethren
questions.explanation: Judges 11:2 shows Jephthah was first expelled by his brethren before the Ammonite war or elders sending for him.

questions.question: True or False: Jephthah gathered vain men to go with him after he fled to the land of Tob.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 11:3 states that vain men gathered to Jephthah and went out with him in the land of Tob.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Judges 11:15-17, why did Jephthah argue that Israel did not unlawfully take the land of the children of Ammon?
options: Because Israel had permission from Moab and Edom to pass through their lands
Because Israel never entered the land of Moab or Ammon, only passing nearby
Because Israel made a treaty with the king of Ammon
Because Israel conquered the land of Ammon by force
questions.correctAnswer: Because Israel never entered the land of Moab or Ammon, only passing nearby
questions.explanation: Jephthah explains in Judges 11:15-18 that Israel did not take the land of Moab or the children of Ammon because they passed by the land of Moab and pitched on the other side of Arnon, which was the border of Moab. He also notes in verse 17 that Israel had requested passage through Edom and Moab but was refused, so they stayed in Kadesh.

questions.question: What was the response of the king of Edom and the king of Moab when Israel requested passage through their lands according to Judges 11:17?
options: They granted permission willingly
They made a treaty with Israel
They refused to let Israel pass through their lands
They ignored Israel's request
questions.correctAnswer: They refused to let Israel pass through their lands
questions.explanation: Judges 11:17 states that Israel sent messengers to the kings of Edom and Moab requesting passage, but both kings refused, and Israel remained in Kadesh.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:18 describe Israel's movement in relation to Moab's border?
options: Israel crossed deep into Moabite territory
Israel camped inside the land of Moab
Israel skirted the east side of Moab and camped on the other side of Arnon
Israel avoided Moab entirely by traveling around Edom
questions.correctAnswer: Israel skirted the east side of Moab and camped on the other side of Arnon
questions.explanation: The passage in Judges 11:18 clarifies that Israel went along the wilderness, compassing Edom and Moab, then camped on the opposite side of the Arnon river, which was the boundary of Moab, without entering Moabite land.

questions.question: Why did Jephthah claim in Judges 11:19-22 that Israel was justified in possessing the land of the Amorites?
options: Because the Amorites sold the land to Israel
Because the LORD delivered the Amorites into Israel's hands after Israel sought passage through their land
Because Israel conquered the Amorites in battle without divine help
Because Israel had a covenant with the Amorites
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD delivered the Amorites into Israel's hands after Israel sought passage through their land
questions.explanation: Jephthah explains in Judges 11:19-22 that Israel asked Sihon, king of the Amorites, for passage, but was refused and attacked. The LORD then delivered Sihon and his people into Israel's hand, allowing Israel to possess the Amorite lands.

questions.question: What argument does Jephthah use in Judges 11:23-24 to challenge the king of Ammon's claim to the land?
options: That the LORD God of Israel had dispossessed the Amorites, so Israel rightfully possessed their land
That the king of Ammon's god Chemosh had no power
That the king of Ammon made a prior treaty with Israel
That Israel had bought the land from the Amorites
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD God of Israel had dispossessed the Amorites, so Israel rightfully possessed their land
questions.explanation: Jephthah asserts in Judges 11:23-24 that since the LORD dispossessed the Amorites before Israel, Israel is entitled to the land, just as the king of Ammon possesses land given by his god Chemosh.

questions.question: In Judges 11:25-26, how does Jephthah question the king of Ammon’s right to fight Israel over the land?
options: By stating that the king of Ammon had never fought against Israel before
By saying Israel had invaded Ammon unjustly
By accusing the king of Ammon of breaking a treaty
By reminding him that Israel had been in the region for 300 years and Ammon never recovered the land
questions.correctAnswer: By reminding him that Israel had been in the region for 300 years and Ammon never recovered the land
questions.explanation: Jephthah challenges the king of Ammon in Judges 11:25-26 by pointing out that Israel had dwelt in the region for 300 years without Ammon recovering the land, implying the king's claim is weak.

questions.question: What does Jephthah request in Judges 11:27 to resolve the dispute between Israel and Ammon?
options: That they go to war immediately
That the LORD, the Judge, be the judge between them
That the matter be settled by a human judge
That they split the land peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD, the Judge, be the judge between them
questions.explanation: In Judges 11:27, Jephthah appeals to the LORD as the ultimate judge to decide the dispute between Israel and the children of Ammon.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 11:28, the king of the children of Ammon accepted Jephthah's words and avoided war.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 11:28 states that the king of the children of Ammon did not listen to Jephthah's words, indicating he rejected the plea and continued in hostility.

questions.question: What promise does Judges 11:29-31 reveal about Jephthah’s vow to the LORD if he was victorious over the children of Ammon?
options: To build a temple for the LORD
To offer as a burnt offering whatever came out of his house to meet him
To dedicate his firstborn son to the LORD
To give half of the spoils of war to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: To offer as a burnt offering whatever came out of his house to meet him
questions.explanation: In Judges 11:30-31, Jephthah vowed to offer as a burnt offering whatever came out of the doors of his house to meet him after his return if the LORD gave him victory over the children of Ammon.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:32-33 describe the outcome of Jephthah’s battle against the children of Ammon?
options: Jephthah was defeated and fled
The LORD delivered the children of Ammon into Jephthah's hands, and Israel defeated them with great slaughter
The battle ended in a stalemate
Jephthah made a peace treaty with Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD delivered the children of Ammon into Jephthah's hands, and Israel defeated them with great slaughter
questions.explanation: Judges 11:32-33 records that the LORD delivered the children of Ammon to Jephthah, who defeated them with a very great slaughter, subduing them before Israel.

questions.question: What was Jephthah’s reaction when his daughter came out to meet him according to Judges 11:34-35?
options: He was joyful and praised God
He rent his clothes and lamented because of his vow
He ignored her and entered the city
He celebrated with a feast
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and lamented because of his vow
questions.explanation: Judges 11:34-35 describes Jephthah’s grief when his daughter, his only child, came out to meet him. He tore his clothes in sorrow, realizing his vow meant he could not take it back.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 11:36, Jephthah’s daughter accepted her father’s vow and urged him to fulfill it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Judges 11:36, Jephthah’s daughter tells her father to do according to his vow because the LORD has taken vengeance on their enemies, showing her acceptance and submission to God’s will.

questions.question: What did Jephthah’s daughter request in Judges 11:37 before fulfilling the vow?
options: To marry a priest
To go up and down the mountains for two months to bewail her virginity with her companions
To flee the town for safety
To hold a festival in her honor
questions.correctAnswer: To go up and down the mountains for two months to bewail her virginity with her companions
questions.explanation: Judges 11:37 shows that she requested two months to mourn her virginity on the mountains with her companions before the vow was fulfilled.

questions.question: What custom in Israel arose from the events of Jephthah’s vow as described in Judges 11:40?
options: Yearly feasts celebrating Jephthah's victory
Annual lamentation by the daughters of Israel for four days
A yearly fast on the day Jephthah returned
A pilgrimage to Mizpeh
questions.correctAnswer: Annual lamentation by the daughters of Israel for four days
questions.explanation: Judges 11:40 states that it became a custom for the daughters of Israel to lament the daughter of Jephthah for four days each year, commemorating her story.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 11:26-27 teaches us about trusting God’s justice when we face wrongful accusations or attacks.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In verses 26-27, Jephthah maintains his integrity by declaring he has not sinned against Ammon and appeals to the LORD, the Judge, to decide the dispute, showing trust in God's justice despite wrongdoing against him.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 11.

questions.question: What happened to Jephthah when the Spirit of the LORD came upon him?
options: He passed over Gilead, Manasseh, and Mizpeh, then went to the children of Ammon
He immediately defeated the children of Ammon without battle
He built an altar to the LORD in Mizpeh
He fled from the land of Tob
questions.correctAnswer: He passed over Gilead, Manasseh, and Mizpeh, then went to the children of Ammon
questions.explanation: Judges 11:29 shows that when the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, he passed over Gilead, Manasseh, Mizpeh, and then to the children of Ammon to confront them.

questions.question: What was the vow Jephthah made to the LORD before going into battle?
options: To offer as a burnt offering whatever came out of his house to meet him
To build a temple if victorious
To never return home if he lost
To give half his spoils to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To offer as a burnt offering whatever came out of his house to meet him
questions.explanation: Judges 11:30-31 records Jephthah's vow that if the LORD delivered the children of Ammon into his hands, whatever came out of his house to meet him would be the LORD's and offered as a burnt offering.

questions.question: How did the LORD assist Jephthah in his battle against the children of Ammon?
options: The LORD delivered the children of Ammon into Jephthah's hands
The LORD sent an angel to fight alongside Jephthah
The LORD blinded the Ammonite army
The LORD caused a famine in Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD delivered the children of Ammon into Jephthah's hands
questions.explanation: Judges 11:32 states that the LORD delivered the children of Ammon into Jephthah's hands, enabling him to defeat them.

questions.question: How many cities did Jephthah defeat in his campaign against the children of Ammon?
options: Twenty cities
Ten cities
Thirty cities
Fifteen cities
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty cities
questions.explanation: According to Judges 11:33, Jephthah smote the children of Ammon from Aroer to Minnith, including twenty cities, showing the extent of his victory.

questions.question: Who met Jephthah when he returned home after the battle?
options: His only daughter with timbrels and dances
His wife with a feast
His sons with gifts
The elders of Gilead with praises
questions.correctAnswer: His only daughter with timbrels and dances
questions.explanation: Judges 11:34 records that Jephthah's only child, his daughter, came out to meet him with timbrels and dances as he returned home.

questions.question: What was Jephthah's reaction upon seeing his daughter after the vow?
options: He rent his clothes and lamented because he could not reverse his vow
He rejoiced in her safety
He ignored her and entered the house
He told her to prepare the burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and lamented because he could not reverse his vow
questions.explanation: Judges 11:35 shows Jephthah tore his clothes and lamented his daughter, recognizing that he was bound by the vow he had made to the LORD.

questions.question: What was the daughter's response to her father's vow?
options: She accepted it and asked for two months to bewail her virginity
She begged him to rescind the vow
She fled to the mountains permanently
She asked to marry before the vow was fulfilled
questions.correctAnswer: She accepted it and asked for two months to bewail her virginity
questions.explanation: Judges 11:36-37 records that Jephthah's daughter accepted the vow and requested two months to roam the mountains and bewail her virginity with her companions.

questions.question: What custom arose in Israel because of Jephthah’s daughter?
options: The daughters of Israel lamented her four days each year
The people held a yearly feast in Mizpeh
Jephthah's family was exempted from military service
The Israelites celebrated a day of fasting
questions.correctAnswer: The daughters of Israel lamented her four days each year
questions.explanation: Judges 11:40 says it became a custom that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament Jephthah's daughter for four days.

questions.question: Which other Biblical passage echoes the theme of a costly vow involving a child as seen in Judges 11?
options: Genesis 22:1-19
Exodus 20:1-17
Psalm 23
Matthew 5:3-12
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 22:1-19
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:1-19 describes Abraham’s test of faith where he was prepared to offer his son Isaac, paralleling the theme of a costly vow and child sacrifice in Judges 11:30-31.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'vow' (נֶדֶר, neder) in the context of Judges 11:30?
options: It denotes a solemn promise with binding religious obligation
It means a casual wish or hope
It refers to a legal contract between tribes
It is a term for a military alliance
questions.correctAnswer: It denotes a solemn promise with binding religious obligation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'neder' used in Judges 11:30 indicates a solemn vow or promise to God that carries a binding religious obligation, explaining why Jephthah felt he could not retract it.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Judges 11:32-40 concerning Jephthah's vow and its consequences?
options: Tragic irony
Parable
Hyperbole
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Tragic irony
questions.explanation: The passage shows tragic irony: Jephthah vows a vow to God for victory, only to have it result in his daughter's sacrifice, an outcome he did not foresee, fulfilling the literary device of tragic irony.

questions.question: What was Jephthah’s argument to the king of the children of Ammon regarding Israel's possession of land?
options: Israel did not take Ammon’s land; they defeated the Amorites as the LORD gave them the land
Israel conquered Ammon through deceit
The land was always Ammonite territory
Israel stole the land unlawfully
questions.correctAnswer: Israel did not take Ammon’s land; they defeated the Amorites as the LORD gave them the land
questions.explanation: Judges 11:15-24 details Jephthah's argument that Israel did not take land from Ammon but from the Amorites, whom the LORD dispossessed, asserting divine approval for Israel's possession.

questions.question: True or False: The elders of Gilead initially rejected Jephthah because he was the son of a harlot.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 11:1-2 explains that Jephthah was thrust out by his brothers because he was the son of a harlot, showing initial rejection.

questions.question: True or False: Jephthah’s daughter was willing to oppose her father’s vow and prevent the sacrifice.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 11:36 shows Jephthah’s daughter accepted the vow and requested time to mourn, indicating submission rather than opposition.

questions.question: What does Jephthah’s crossing over Gilead and Manasseh before reaching Mizpeh suggest about his leadership journey?
options: It symbolizes a strategic military and spiritual preparation before battle
It was a ritual pilgrimage to seek forgiveness
It indicates his exile route back home
It was a trek to gather reinforcements
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a strategic military and spiritual preparation before battle
questions.explanation: Judges 11:29 portrays Jephthah’s journey through these territories as both a physical and symbolic preparation for leadership and battle, marking a transition from exile to commander.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is primarily demonstrated by Jephthah's vow in Judges 11:30-31?
options: The doctrine of sanctification through works
The doctrine of the seriousness of vows before God
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the seriousness of vows before God
questions.explanation: Judges 11:30-31 shows Jephthah making a solemn vow to the LORD that he must keep regardless of personal cost, illustrating the biblical principle that vows made before God are binding and must be fulfilled.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:21 reveal the attribute of God's providence in Israel's military victory?
options: God's omniscience in knowing the battle plans
God's providential deliverance of Israel over Sihon
God's wrath against Israel
God's indifference to Israel's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential deliverance of Israel over Sihon
questions.explanation: Judges 11:21 explicitly states that 'the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel,' demonstrating God's providential care and intervention in Israel's conquest.

questions.question: What does the rejection of Jephthah by his brothers in Judges 11:2 teach about human sin and rejection in the biblical narrative?
options: It demonstrates the universal human experience of rejection due to sin
It shows that only perfect people are accepted by God
It teaches that human rejection has no spiritual consequences
It reveals God's approval of family disputes
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the universal human experience of rejection due to sin
questions.explanation: In Judges 11:2, Jephthah is rejected by his brothers because of his birth from a harlot, illustrating how sin and societal prejudice often lead to human rejection, a theme that reveals the brokenness of humanity.

questions.question: How do Judges 11:5-6 and Judges 11:11 together teach about God's use of flawed human instruments for deliverance?
options: God only uses perfect individuals for leadership
God chooses even the outcast Jephthah as leader to save Israel
God rejects those with sinful backgrounds for leadership roles
God relies solely on angelic beings for Israel's deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: God chooses even the outcast Jephthah as leader to save Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 show elders seeking Jephthah despite his past rejection, and verse 11 shows him made captain, indicating God’s sovereign choice of flawed individuals to accomplish His purposes (cf. 1 Corinthians 1:27).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Judges 11:29 where the Spirit of the LORD comes upon Jephthah?
options: God's omnipresence
God's empowering presence for leadership
God's wrathful judgment
God's hiddenness
questions.correctAnswer: God's empowering presence for leadership
questions.explanation: Judges 11:29 reveals that the Spirit of the LORD empowered Jephthah to lead in battle, showing God's attribute of empowering His servants to fulfill His will.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:23-24 reflect the theological principle of divine sovereignty over land possession?
options: Land is possessed only by human might and strategy
God grants and dispossesses land according to His divine will
Land ownership is irrelevant in the biblical narrative
Possession of land is a result of economic prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: God grants and dispossesses land according to His divine will
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 affirm that the LORD God of Israel dispossessed the Amorites and grants land to His people, emphasizing divine sovereignty over territorial inheritance.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Judges 11:7 and Judges 11:9 provide regarding human distrust and divine calling?
options: Distrust invalidates divine calling
Human distrust can coexist with God's call to leadership and responsibility
Divine calling is based on human perfection
Distrust leads to rejection of God's mission
questions.correctAnswer: Human distrust can coexist with God's call to leadership and responsibility
questions.explanation: In verse 7, Jephthah recalls past rejection and distrust by his brothers, yet in verse 9 he negotiates terms to lead, illustrating that human distrust does not negate God's call on a person’s life.

questions.question: What does Judges 11:13-18 teach about Israel’s respect for divine boundaries and neighborly relations?
options: Israel unlawfully took Moabite and Ammonite lands
Israel respected the borders of Moab and Ammon, abiding by God-ordained boundaries
Israel ignored all boundaries and took land by force
Israel had no knowledge of territorial borders
questions.correctAnswer: Israel respected the borders of Moab and Ammon, abiding by God-ordained boundaries
questions.explanation: These verses narrate Israel’s request to pass through lands and their respect for Moab and Ammon's borders, highlighting obedience to divine boundaries.

questions.question: In what way does Judges 11:34-39 illustrate the tension between human vows and divine mercy?
options: It shows that human vows override divine mercy
It reveals the tragic cost when human vows are made without divine guidance
It demonstrates that God always prevents human tragedy
It teaches that vows are optional in worship
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the tragic cost when human vows are made without divine guidance
questions.explanation: Jephthah's vow results in the loss of his daughter (verses 34-39), showing the tragic consequences of rash vows and the tension between human promises and God's mercy.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:28 serve as an apologetics point against the claim that God’s prophets always succeed in persuading enemies to peace?
options: It confirms that all enemies repent after hearing God's messenger
It shows that God’s messengers may be rejected, yet God's purposes prevail
It indicates that God forces all enemies to peace
It implies God’s messengers never confront enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that God’s messengers may be rejected, yet God's purposes prevail
questions.explanation: Verse 28 states the Ammonite king ignored Jephthah's message, refuting the skeptic's idea that God’s word always leads to peace, yet God's sovereign will still triumphs.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about divine justice can be inferred from Judges 11:27 and Judges 11:32-33 taken together?
options: Divine justice is arbitrary and unpredictable
God judges between Israel and Ammon and delivers Israel victoriously
Human warfare determines divine justice
Divine justice is irrelevant in earthly conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: God judges between Israel and Ammon and delivers Israel victoriously
questions.explanation: Verse 27 appeals to the LORD as judge between Israel and Ammon, and verses 32-33 confirm God delivering Israel, teaching that divine justice is active and decisive in history.

questions.question: What narrative connection does Judges 11:1-3 establish about human sin and God's redemptive use of flawed individuals?
options: God only uses perfect people for His purposes
God often uses outcasts like Jephthah to accomplish His redemptive plans
Jephthah's birth disqualifies him from leadership
Human sin always prevents divine salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God often uses outcasts like Jephthah to accomplish His redemptive plans
questions.explanation: These verses introduce Jephthah as a son of a harlot who was rejected but later used by God, illustrating how God redeems flawed humans for His purposes.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:35-36 reflect the biblical theme of submission to God's sovereign will even in personal suffering?
options: Jephthah rebels against God's will
Jephthah and his daughter accept the consequences of his vow as God's judgment
Jephthah ignores the vow
Jephthah negotiates to avoid suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Jephthah and his daughter accept the consequences of his vow as God's judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 35-36 show Jephthah’s anguish and his daughter’s willing acceptance of the vow’s outcome, demonstrating submission to God’s sovereign will despite personal pain.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Judges 11:12-13 and Judges 11:25-26 reveal about Israel’s rightful claim to land and defense against accusations?
options: Israel unjustly took land from Ammon
Israel’s possession of land is based on God’s providence and historical tenure
Israel has no claim to any land
Israel’s land claims are based on conquest alone
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s possession of land is based on God’s providence and historical tenure
questions.explanation: In 11:12-13 Ammon accuses Israel of taking their land, but 11:25-26 Jephthah counters by highlighting Israel’s long tenure and divine dispossession of others, affirming God’s providential grant of land.

questions.question: How does Judges 11:40, concerning the yearly lament for Jephthah’s daughter, contribute to understanding Israel's cultic remembrance practices?
options: It shows Israel ignored personal tragedies
It demonstrates a formalized communal lament as a form of remembrance and repentance
It reveals a joyful celebration
It indicates no remembrance of past events
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates a formalized communal lament as a form of remembrance and repentance
questions.explanation: Verse 40 states daughters of Israel annually lament Jephthah's daughter for four days, showing a ritualized remembrance reflecting sorrow and communal repentance.
